findings.description: After an ordinary rollback Storage result, the test unconditionally reads journal.v1 and requires retained ROLLED_BACK. The adopted contract allows cleanup after verified rollback, deleting owned artifacts and journal last. Thus a conforming implementation can fail this postcondition because it completed valid cleanup. The existing first assertion RED remains genuine, but that does not validate later assertions.
findings.required_action: Use existing test-only observation callback at an approved pre-cleanup checkpoint to capture and independently validate verified ROLLED_BACK. Separately assert final formal bytes/absence, preservation and either valid retained terminal state or completed owned cleanup. Add an explicit normal rollback-cleanup-success row; do not simply delete terminal evidence assertions.
findings.blocks: Module-contract readiness, not observed first-assertion RED validity

findings.description: The generic cleanup.remove failure case requires old.bin to remain even after formal OLD has been restored and verified. The approved rule protects the unique preimage, not a particular redundant copy or deletion order. A legal cleanup can delete redundant old.bin, fail deleting new.bin, retain verified journal, and preserve formal OLD. This test forbids that legal order.
conforming_counterexample: return error consistent with verified rollback
findings.test_result_for_counterexample: old.bin.exists() assertion fails although no unique preimage or foreign data is lost
findings.required_action: Define which artifact the fault targets or allow both safe cleanup orders. Assert verified formal preimage, terminal evidence, foreign preservation and remaining artifact integrity. Test unique-preimage preservation separately at an actual unverified-restoration failure.

findings.description: For unparseable/unknown/checksum-invalid records the contract requires old/new diagnostics None until safe artifacts have been verified. Current assertions accept Some paths if they have the expected safe parent/basename; a decoder can therefore fabricate old.bin/new.bin diagnostic provenance and still pass all these assertions. Safe path syntax is not verification of the referenced version.
findings.counterexample: For invalid magic or checksum return RecoveryRequired with target/journal correct, reason nonempty, old_version_path=Some(area/old.bin), new_version_path=Some(area/new.bin), without decoding or validating either artifact. Current diagnostic assertions accept this.
findings.required_action: For the unmistakably pre-parse cases (bad magic, unsupported version, invalid checksum/framing/oversize), explicitly require old_version_path=None and new_version_path=None. Maintain separate assertions for the valid-record/verified-artifact cases that may legitimately provide paths.
findings.blocks: Diagnostic contract coverage; existing RED classification remains genuine
